newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Office recovers after sell-off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Office recovers after sell-off.

text.p: U.S. Office Products Co's share price was up 2-1/4 to 28 Wednesday, recouping most its Tuesday drop of 2-7/8.
Analysts said yesterday's decline was sparked by rumors related to Federal Trade Commission opposition to the proposed merger of U.S. Office Products competitors Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc.
"There are some rumors floating around," said Susan Lacerra, senior analyst at Robertson Stephens. "One rumor is that U.S. Office Products would buy Office Depot."
She was skeptical. "But Office Depot is a turnaround company. That is not something I believe U.S. Office Products would get involved in," she said. "They wouldn't buy a turnaround company."
Lacerra added, "I think the stock (U.S. Office Products) is totally undervalued at these levels."
On Monday the FTC voted to block the Staples-Office Depot merger. The companies said they would fight to preserve the deal.
Lehman Brothers analyst William Julian, in a research report this morning, cited a rumor that the FTC would tighten scrutiny of U.S. Office Products deals.
He said another rumor held that the company might buy stores divested by Staples and Office Depot in an effort to appease the FTC.
"We believe...rumors driving the (stock lower are) all completely off the mark," Julian said in the report. "We would be aggressive buyers of the stock at these prices."
Lacerra said shares of U.S. Office Products began a descent two weeks ago, when competitor Corporate Express Inc announced that its fourth quarter earnings would be below expectations.
"U.S. Office Products was tarred with the same brush," she said.
Lacerra said Corporate Express's problems were in its delivery business, not its office products business.
"Corporate Express said that its office products business is doing well," she said.
